findings.title: Invalid activity timestamp crashes entire dashboard render
evidence: Backend returns an activity with createdAt = null, undefined, or an unparseable string.
Page renders the Recent Activities list and executes `new Date(activity.createdAt)` (line ~626), producing an Invalid Date object.
`formatDistanceToNow` receives the Invalid Date and calls `date.getTime()` (format-date.ts), returning NaN.
The function falls through all divisions with NaN and calls `relativeTimeFormatter.format(Math.round(NaN), 'years')`.
`Intl.RelativeTimeFormat.format` throws a RangeError because NaN is not a finite number, causing a full white-screen React error boundary crash on the dashboard.
Same path exists for upcoming activities via `format(new Date(activity.dueAt), 'MMM d, yyyy')` (line ~645), where `Intl.DateTimeFormat.format` on an Invalid Date also throws.
findings.fix_hint: Validate or coerce activity timestamps at the API/query boundary, or make the formatters return a safe fallback for Invalid Date instead of throwing.

findings.title: Hardcoded route strings create a silent 404 cascade if any route is renamed
evidence: KPI cards, empty states, activity links, and the imported InsightsWidget all use literal href strings: `/invoices`, `/deals`, `/products/new`, `/activities`.
Next.js does not type-check string literals in a standard app router setup, so renaming a directory from `deals` to `sales` compiles cleanly while leaving every card pointing to a dead route.
Users clicking the polished KPI cards land on a 404 page instead of the expected surface, breaking the primary navigation affordance of the dashboard.
Because the strings are scattered across the page component and child components (EmptyState, InsightsWidget), a refactor is likely to miss one or more occurrences.

findings.title: Whole-card Link wraps create a nested-interactive trap for any future action
evidence: Each KPI card is currently rendered as `<Link href='...' className='group block'><Card>...</Card></Link>` (lines ~311, ~329, ~347, ~365, ~383, ~406).
The Card currently contains only static content, so there is no immediate nested-anchor violation.
A later feature request adds an inline action inside a card—e.g., a 'Copy value', 'Refresh', or 'Filter' button, or a second mini-link.

That new interactive element is now a descendant of an `<a>` tag, which violates HTML content models and causes: split click targets, Next.js hydration warnings, screen-reader confusion, and unpredictable event routing.
The page design creates a fragile contract: any future enhancement inside a KPI card must remember not to add buttons or links.

findings.title: Activity rows link to the generic list instead of the specific record
evidence: Recent and Upcoming Activities render each activity as a clickable row containing the activity title and timestamp.
Every row is wrapped in `<Link href='/activities'>`, so clicking 'Call with Acme Corp' navigates to `/activities`, not the detail view of that activity.
The visual affordance (a full-width, hover-highlighted row with a title) trains users to expect record-level navigation, but the behavior is list-level navigation.
Users repeatedly lose context: they click an activity, arrive at the list, then must scroll/search to re-find the item they just clicked.
This is normal, legitimate use that produces emergent friction rather than an error.

findings.title: Rapid date-range switching causes a thundering herd of concurrent refetches
evidence: The date-range Select uses `onValueChange={(v) => setRange(v as DateRange)}` (line ~270) with no debounce.
The page subscribes to eight separate `useAuthQuery` hooks; changing range triggers refetches across all of them.
A user rapidly cycles through ranges (e.g., this month → last month → this quarter → this year), issuing up to 32 concurrent requests in a short window.
If in-flight Convex subscriptions are not cancelled or deduplicated, older responses can overwrite newer selection state or cause UI jank on slow networks.
No loading skeleton or request cancellation feedback is shown during the transition, so the dashboard feels unresponsive.

findings.title: InsightsWidget silently drops due-soon activities when dueAt is an ISO string
evidence: The page imports and renders `<InsightsWidget overview={overview} />` (line ~424).
Inside InsightsWidget, the due-soon filter computes `const diff = a.dueAt - now` and checks `diff > 0 && diff < 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000`.
If the API returns `dueAt` as an ISO string (a common shape), subtracting a number from a string yields `NaN`.
`NaN > 0 && NaN < 86400000` is always false, so urgent activities due within 24 hours are filtered out silently.

The same activities render correctly in the Upcoming Activities list because that code wraps `dueAt` in `new Date(activity.dueAt)`, creating a composition mismatch where one component understands the type and another does not.
Result: users miss high-priority items in the insights banner even though the data exists.
findings.fix_hint: Normalize timestamps in the dashboard query hook or inside InsightsWidget so both consumers operate on Date objects or numeric timestamps consistently.

residual_risks: The `forecastData?.map((s: any) => ({ ... }))` path uses `any`, so malformed backend responses for stage/dealCount/totalValue can propagate into PipelineChart as undefined or NaN.
testing_gaps: No test asserts that malformed activity timestamps do not crash the dashboard render.
No test verifies that all dashboard hrefs resolve to real application routes.
No test simulates rapid date-range changes to confirm no stale-state overwrite or request thrashing.
No a11y test checks that Link-wrapped cards contain no nested interactive elements.
